workflow_instructions.mode_overview: This mode is for developers working on GPU programming and high‑performance computing in Sounio. It covers GPU kernels, backends (PTX, SPIR‑V, Metal), embedding C ABI, and performance optimizations for parallel hardware.

step.details: Determine whether the change involves: - GPU kernel definitions (`kernel fn`) and launch semantics - Backend‑specific code generation (PTX, SPIR‑V, Metal) - Device memory management and synchronization - Embedding C interface (`sounio_embed.h`) for host integration - Performance profiling or optimization

Review the relevant source areas: - Read `self‑hosted/gpu/` for backend implementation - Examine `stdlib/gpu/` for GPU‑specific library functions - Check the embedding header `interop/embed/sounio_embed.h` - Look at GPU examples under `examples/`

phase.name: analysis
phase.description: Analyze the current implementation and plan the change

steps.step: Identify which GPU backend or kernel component is affected
Understand the target hardware capabilities (CUDA, Metal, Vulkan)
Check existing GPU tests and examples for expected behavior
Consider performance implications and potential regressions
Edit the GPU backend source files or kernel definitions
Ensure kernel launch parameters (grid, block) are valid
Update embedding ABI if host‑device communication changes
Run the GPU test suite (if available) and compile GPU examples
Generate PTX/SPIR‑V output and inspect for correctness
Test embedding integration with a simple host program
Check that the change does not break non‑GPU backends

completion_criteria.criterion: The requested GPU/HPC functionality is implemented
GPU kernels compile and produce valid backend code
Embedding interface remains stable and functional
Documentation (comments, examples) is updated if needed
